# Message codes: Files and size caps

See also: [Message codes](message-codes.md) (the index of every code) and
[Messages and codes](messages.md) (the line grammar, what a code guarantees and
when to trust one).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_message_reference.py; do not edit. -->

Trust a code only when the line is one of the lines below, a value in place of
each `<name>`, after at most one prefix: the index lists the prefixes and
`message-codes-values.md` the values.

## Codes

| Code | Level | Means | Since |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`dir-unlistable`](#dir-unlistable) | ERROR, WARNING | A directory could not be listed (no read or search permission): the files under it were not seen. The ERROR line, for a directory named as a 'loom id generate' PATH, prints since 0.25.0. | 0.22.0 |

A path named for Pitloom to read (a wheel, a project, a configuration, an ID registry, an SBOM) under a directory without search permission says so 'for the input check', not that it is not found. The ERROR line for an SBOM given to 'loom id import' or to embed, for an ID registry file, for a 'loom id generate' PATH, for a configuration file and for the input check, prints since 0.25.0. ### `dir-unlistable`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A directory could not be listed (no read or search permission): the
  files under it were not seen. The ERROR line, for a directory named as a 'loom
  id generate' PATH, prints since 0.25.0.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Went on without them: file discovery leaves them out of the
  SBOM (a build backend that lists before it excludes can name a directory it
  would leave out anyway); a dataset directory gets no hash (Evidence:
  not_measured | Reason: dir-unlistable); ID registry indexing leaves them out
  of the index; a model or dataset card in it is not found. As an ERROR (a
  directory named as a PATH to index), 'loom id generate' writes no registry and
  exits 1, and the library raises ValueError carrying the code.
- **Tell the user**: which directory could not be listed and what the system
  reported, as the line says. They give the account Pitloom runs as read and
  search access to it and generate again. Do not change permissions or
  ownership, or copy or move files, for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask,
  report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: could not list <use>; <failure> [dir-unlistable]
  ERROR: DIR=<dir>: could not list <use>; <failure> [dir-unlistable]
  ```

### `file-unreadable`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A file Pitloom found or was named could not be read: the operating
  system refused it (no read permission, a directory above it without search
  permission, a file another program holds open on Windows) or the read failed
  (an I/O error, a file that is no regular file once opened). A path named for
  Pitloom to read (a wheel, a project, a configuration, an ID registry, an SBOM)
  under a directory without search permission says so 'for the input check', not
  that it is not found. The ERROR line for an SBOM given to 'loom id import' or
  to embed, for an ID registry file, for a 'loom id generate' PATH, for a
  configuration file and for the input check, prints since 0.25.0. A wheel given
  to verify-wheel, validate-wheel or embed-wheel that the system refuses is said
  'for the SBOM'. The DIR= line is a loom dataset directory whose dataset card
  could not be read for a reason that names no file of it; as an ERROR (since
  0.25.0), DIR=. is the current directory, gone or not readable, where Pitloom
  resolves a path against it.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Read nothing more of it and went on without what it holds, as
  the line says what it was read for: a file scan leaves the file out of the
  SBOM (loom embed-wheel keeps it, with the wheel's own hash); a hash leaves no
  verifiedUsing (a model's ID registry lookup is then not gated; a dataset's
  provenance says Evidence: not_measured | Reason: file-unreadable); a project
  setting's field is not set from the file; the usage scan records no model
  reference from it; ID registry indexing leaves it out of the index; an ID
  registry file read again to save the ids a run added is not saved; no
  dependency pins are read from a lock file; a model whose header could not be
  read is not listed as an AI model; a model or dataset card (the DIR= line too)
  sets none of the fields it states; installed project metadata is ignored, and
  a setup.cfg or setup.py read beside another source leaves the project read
  without it. As an ERROR, the call that named the file raises (a Croissant
  document: the dataset declaration fails; an SBOM to import: the ID registry is
  not written; an SBOM to embed: no wheel is changed; an ID registry file, or a
  'loom id generate' PATH: no registry or SBOM is written; a configuration file,
  or a project metadata file (a project's pyproject.toml read by the build hook
  says for the configuration): nothing is written; the only possible model file
  of a folder named for a model SBOM: no SBOM is written; the input check: the
  command writes nothing and exits 1, the library raises ValueError carrying the
  code; the current directory: the command writes nothing and exits 1, the
  library and the loom SDK raise ValueError carrying the code; a wheel of
  verify-wheel, validate-wheel or embed-wheel fails alone, the others go on).
- **Tell the user**: which file could not be read and what the system reported,
  as the line says. They give the account Pitloom runs as read access to it (or
  close the program that holds it), or restore a damaged copy, and generate
  again. Do not change permissions or ownership, or copy, move or replace the
  file, for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: could not read <use>; <failure> [file-unreadable]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: could not read for <field>; <failure> [file-unreadable]
  WARNING: FORMAT=<format> FILE=<file>: could not read header; <failure> [file-unreadable]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: could not read <use>; <failure> [file-unreadable]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: could not read <use>; <failure> [file-unreadable]
  ERROR: FORMAT=<format> FILE=<file>: could not read header; <failure> [file-unreadable]
  ERROR: DIR=<dir>: could not read <use>; <failure> [file-unreadable]
  ```

### `file-unreadable/not-utf8`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A text file Pitloom read is not UTF-8, the encoding it must be in:
  a requirements file or a file a setup.cfg directive lists, a Python file read
  for the model usage scan (a WARNING:), or an SBOM given to embed or to import
  into an ID registry, an ID registry file (an ERROR:, which prints since
  0.25.0), or a configuration file (an ERROR:).
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Went on without what the file holds: the field is not set
  from it, or the usage scan records no model reference from it; an sdist's
  pyproject.toml read only for its declared authors gives them from PKG-INFO,
  without their declared order. For an SBOM, wrote nothing: to embed, no wheel
  is changed; to import, the ID registry is not written. For an ID registry file
  or a configuration file, wrote nothing: no registry and no SBOM.
- **Tell the user**: which file is not UTF-8 and what the decoder reported, as
  the line says. They save it as UTF-8 (an SBOM: generate it again) and run
  again. Do not convert, edit or replace the file for them; ask first, and with
  nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: could not read <use>; not UTF-8: <failure> [file-unreadable/not-utf8]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: could not read for <field>; not UTF-8: <failure> [file-unreadable/not-utf8]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: could not read <use>; not UTF-8: <failure> [file-unreadable/not-utf8]
  ```

### `file-unreadable/outside-project`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: A file a project setting names, or a licence file, leads outside
  the project directory (a .. or absolute path, or a symbolic link out), and
  Pitloom reads no file outside it: its content is no part of the project. For
  an installed dependency, the directory is its .dist-info.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Did not read it and went on without what it holds: the field
  is not set from it, or its licence text and copyright notices are not used.
- **Tell the user**: which file lies outside the project and which setting or
  licence file names it, as the line says. They move or copy the file into the
  project, or point the setting at a file inside it, and generate again; for an
  installed dependency, only its maintainers can fix it. Do not move, copy or
  link files, or edit the setting, for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask,
  report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: could not read <use>; outside the project directory [file-unreadable/outside-project]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: could not read for <field>; outside the project directory [file-unreadable/outside-project]
  ```

### `file-unreadable/outside-repository`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: The build configuration of a project fetched from a Git URL lists
  files outside the downloaded repository (an absolute or .. path, as in a
  Hatchling force-include, or its .git directory), and Pitloom reads no file
  outside it: the repository is untrusted, and such a file is the host's. A
  setting entry left out before the files are listed is named as the
  configuration writes it, one line each; files left out once listed are only
  counted, never named.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Did not read them and left them out of the SBOM: no hash, no
  copyright or licence text from their headers, no AI model metadata.
- **Tell the user**: that the repository's build configuration names files
  outside it, which were left out, as the line says. To have them in the SBOM,
  they clone the repository, check what those paths name, and generate from the
  local copy. Do not clone or run on a local copy for them; ask first, and with
  nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: outside the downloaded repository; not read [file-unreadable/outside-repository]
  WARNING: listed files outside the downloaded repository<count>; not read [file-unreadable/outside-repository]
  ```

### `file-unwritable`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A file Pitloom writes could not be written: the operating system
  refused it (no write permission on the file or its directory, a read-only file
  system, a full disk, a directory where the file should be). The ID registry
  file, written 'for the ID registry'; a wheel an embed rewrites with its SBOM,
  the SBOM a command writes to '-o' (a library call's output_path), or the SBOM
  the Hatchling build hook stages, written 'for the SBOM'; the fragment a loom
  SDK run writes at its end, written 'for the SBOM fragment'.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Tried to write an ID registry file through a temporary file
  beside it, so a failed write leaves its old content; where the directory
  refuses a temporary file, the file is written in place and a failure (a full
  disk) can leave it part-written. A wheel is written as a new file beside it,
  put in its place once complete: a refused write leaves the wheel as it was; an
  SBOM's '-o' file is written in place (an embed's after the wheel), the hook's
  in a new temporary directory. A loom run's fragment is written in place. As an
  ERROR ('loom id generate', 'loom id import', a command writing its SBOM to
  '-o', the build hook, a loom run), the command exits 1, the build fails or the
  loom run raises OSError carrying the code (an embed-wheel batch goes on with
  its other wheels). As a WARNING (loom generate (a project, wheel or
  environment), project, wheel and env, the library's generate_project_sbom,
  generate_wheel_sbom, generate_env_sbom and the PyPI and Git URL functions that
  call them, and loom.Run, saving the ids a run added after its SBOM is built),
  the SBOM stands and the ids are not saved: the next run mints them again.
- **Tell the user**: which file could not be written and what the system
  reported, as the line says. They give the account Pitloom runs as write access
  to the file and its directory, or free disk space, and run again. Do not
  change permissions or ownership, or delete files, for them; ask first, and
  with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: could not write <use>; <failure> [file-unwritable]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: could not write <use>; <failure> [file-unwritable]
  ```

### `file-unwritable/mode`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: An embed wrote the wheel with its SBOM through a new file put in
  place of the old one, then could not give it the old file's mode (its
  permission bits): the operating system refused (a file system without POSIX
  modes, a file owned by another account).
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Kept the new wheel, SBOM embedded, with the mode a new file
  gets (the umask's); the exit status does not change.
- **Tell the user**: the wheel's permissions changed, as the line says, if they
  rely on them (an executable bit, a group's access). They set the mode again.
  Do not change permissions for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report
  it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: file mode not restored; <failure> [file-unwritable/mode]
  ```

### `over-cap`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: An input is larger than a cap Pitloom puts on what it reads or
  records, so that a crafted or unusually large input cannot exhaust time,
  memory or disk.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Kept what fits the cap and left the rest out, or did not read
  the input; the text after the semicolon says which.
- **Tell the user**: which input was over which cap and what the SBOM lacks for
  it. Four caps are settings, which they can raise for an input they trust and
  then generate again: max-model-extract-bytes (and with it the per-wheel
  model-scan budget, four times it) by --max-model-extract-bytes or its
  [tool.pitloom] key; max-download-bytes (a wheel or sdist downloaded from a
  PyPI URL, a Git URL's checkout, or each metadata file of a Hugging Face
  repository) by --max-download-bytes or its key (each Hugging Face file also
  has its own fixed cap, Hub-JSON, model-card, license-detection or
  dataset-card, which raising the setting does not lift); max-dataset-hash-bytes
  by its key, by --max-dataset-hash-bytes of loom id generate or by the
  max_dataset_hash_bytes argument of loom.Run; max-source-metadata-bytes (the
  artifact-metadata annotation, the model's metadata as read) by
  --max-source-metadata-bytes or its [tool.pitloom.provenance] key, 0 for no
  cap. Every other cap is fixed. Do not raise a cap or generate again for them;
  ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: <key>=<name>: larger than the <limit>-<unit> <cap> cap; <outcome> [over-cap]
  WARNING: FORMAT=<format> FILE=<file>: larger than the <limit>-<unit> <cap> cap; <outcome> [over-cap]
  ERROR: config file '<path>': larger than the <limit>-<unit> <cap> cap; not read [over-cap]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: larger than the <limit>-<unit> <cap> cap <use>; not read [over-cap]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: larger than the <limit>-<unit> <cap> cap; not downloaded [over-cap]
  ERROR: the repository is larger than the <limit>-<unit> <cap> cap; git <command> was stopped [over-cap]
  ERROR: git <command> produced more than <size> [over-cap]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: larger than the <limit>-<unit> <cap> cap <use>; not read [over-cap]
  ```

### `temp-dir-unusable`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A file downloaded from PyPI or a Hugging Face repository could not
  be written to the temporary directory: the disk is full, the path is too long
  (Windows), or the directory cannot be written to.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Stopped the download and wrote no SBOM (the error:
  pypi.save-failed); for a Hugging Face file, left that file out and read the
  rest (the warning).
- **Tell the user**: the download could not be saved locally, with the reason
  the line gives; the network is not the cause. They free disk space, or set
  TMPDIR (TEMP on Windows) to a writable directory with a short path, and run
  again. Do not change their temporary directory for them; ask first, and with
  nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: could not be saved in the temporary directory (<failure>); not downloaded [temp-dir-unusable]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: could not be saved in the temporary directory (<failure>); <outcome> [temp-dir-unusable]
  ```
